newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire parliament rejects Mobutu ally as speaker.
newsitem.headline: Zaire parliament rejects Mobutu ally as speaker.

text.p: Zairean legislators on Wednesday rejected a move by political leaders to place an ally of President Mobutu Sese Seko in the key position of parliament speaker, the constitutional successor to the president.
"There has been no consensus around Mandungu Bula Nyati," deputy speaker of parliament, Andre Boboliko Okonga, said after legislators voted overwhelmingly against the motion.

"The political class is invited to deal with this problem. But the debate has shown that we need a neutral person who does not come from any of the two political families (opposition and presidential movement)," Boboliko added.
Mandungu Bula Nyati is a close ally of Mobutu and a former leader of the ailing president's parliamentary movement.

He was selected last weekend as candidate for the post of speaker, vacant since Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo was ousted in 1995 by a coalition of politicians from the opposition and presidential movements.
According to Zaire's transitional constitution the speaker of parliament succeeds the president in the interim in the event of his death or incapacity.
Mobutu, 66, is battling against prostate cancer as well as a seven-month old rebellion to end his three-decade rule.
